name: Omega-3 fatty acids
short: Linked to a higher risk of atrial fibrillation in cardiovascular trials, more so above 1 g/day; diarrhoea and altered taste were more likely than with placebo; bleeding findings are mixed.
text: In a meta-analysis of 7 cardiovascular outcome trials (81,210 people), marine omega-3 supplements were associated with an increased risk of atrial fibrillation, greater in trials testing more than 1 g/day. A meta-analysis of 90 randomized trials found higher odds of diarrhoea, altered taste and bleeding tendency than with placebo, with no definite related serious adverse events. A separate meta-analysis of 11 trials (120,643 patients) found no overall increase in bleeding, though high-dose purified EPA carried a modest extra risk; background antiplatelet therapy was not associated with bleeding risk in that analysis.

quotes: In RCTs examining cardiovascular outcomes, marine ɷ-3 supplementation was associated with an increased risk of AF. The risk appeared to be greater in trials testing >1 g/d.
citations.label: Gencer et al., 2021, Circulation
citations.title: Effect of Long-Term Marine ɷ-3 Fatty Acids Supplementation on the Risk of Atrial Fibrillation in Randomized Controlled Trials of Cardiovascular Outcomes: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

quotes: A total of 90 RCTs showed that the ω-3 PUFA group, when compared with the placebo, had significantly higher odds of occurrence of diarrhea (odds ratio [OR] = 1.257, P = 0.010), dysgeusia (OR = 3.478, P < 0.001), and bleeding tendency (OR = 1.260, P = 0.025)
There was no report of definite ω-3 PUFA-related serious adverse events.
citations.label: Chang et al., 2023, Adv Nutr
citations.title: Safety of Supplementation of Omega-3 Polyunsaturated Fatty Acids: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.

quotes: A total of 120 643 patients from 11 randomized clinical trials were included.
Omega-3 PUFAs were not associated with increased bleeding risk. Patients receiving high-dose purified EPA may incur additional bleeding risk, although its clinical significance is very modest.
but not the background use of antiplatelet therapy
